extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, contributors and staff of The Texas Tribune (including contractors and interns)
extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom code of ethics and editorial policy for a nonprofit, nonpartisan news organization describing standards for accuracy, sourcing, conflicts of interest, sponsorships/advertising, and AI use. Intended to guide Tribune journalists, editors and staff in producing and publishing journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / Nonpartisanship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Tribune is a nonpartisan, nonprofit media organization whose mission is to provide readers with impartial, informative reporting and an outlet for civic engagement and discourse on public policy, politics, government and other matters of statewide concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mission drives the values and guidelines in the code; exceptional circumstances may require exceptions, and the code will be revised as the industry and technology evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on all platforms will be truthful, transparent and respectful; facts will be accurate, complete and fairly presented. Analysis will represent the newsroom's best independent judgment, not preferences or those of sources; there will be no hidden agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must attribute sources properly and ensure analyses reflect independent judgment rather than source bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When we make a mistake we will work quickly to fully address the error, correcting it within the story, detailing the error on the story page and adding it to a running list of Tribune corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If readers find an error they should email corrections@texastribune.org. Corrections should be visible on the story page and added to the public corrections list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republishing and Attribution of Outside Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribune journalists will not republish stories, images or other content from outside sources without permission and credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain permission and provide clear credit when using outside content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism, Fabrication and Misappropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism, fabrication and misappropriation of intellectual property are all grounds for immediate termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition; violations have immediate, severe employment consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo/Video/Audio Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo editors and video producers may improve the technical quality of photos and video or audio recordings, but may not alter the substance of that media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All photo illustrations, graphics or animations must be clearly labeled as such. The Tribune does not alter substantive elements of multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source Identification and Anonymity Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune will try to identify all sources, granting individuals anonymity only when the information is critical to the story, the source is reliable and there is no other way to obtain the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As much as possible, identify any known bias of sources. Anonymous sources should know the reporter will share their identity with a senior editor who will also keep it confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quoting Anonymous Sources / Declined Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not say that a person declined comment if they are already quoted anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implying a source refused comment when they have been cited anonymously; be transparent about the circumstances of anonymous quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Deception of Sources; No Undercover Tactics or Payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists will never misrepresent themselves or mislead a source to get an interview or a story, and they will always identify themselves as journalists. They do not use hidden cameras or microphones, go undercover or pay for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Straightforward sourcing practices only; no clandestine or paid-sourcing methods permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Multiple Efforts to Contact Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple efforts will be made to contact the primary subjects and sources of criticism in our stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable attempts to reach subjects and critics are required before publishing critical material about them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Independence / Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no sacred cows; the Tribune aggressively pursues all stories it deems newsworthy. Editorial decisions are made by journalists alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain editorial independence from business, fundraising, and outside influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor Non-Entitlement and Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who contribute do so with the understanding that contributions do not entitle them to preferential treatment or relationships with newsroom staff and do not protect them from investigations or scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contributions are listed by year and amount and published publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of Fundraising and Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters play no role in cultivating financial relationships with major donors or corporate sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundraising is handled by non-newsroom business staff to preserve editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure for Stories Referencing Donors/Sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that reference or quote a Tribune donor or corporate sponsor who has contributed $1,000 or more will include a written disclosure that conveys when those stories are picked up by other news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written disclosure should accompany stories referencing significant donors/sponsors to maintain transparency across republications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Work on Stories with Vested Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists may not work on stories or projects in which they have a vested interest, financial or personal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assignments where personal or financial interests could compromise impartial reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Investments in Covered Companies/Industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should avoid investment in companies or industries they regularly cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal financial investments that create conflicts with reporting beats should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Employment and Freelance Clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists seeking secondary employment or freelance work to supplement their income must be cleared by an editor to ensure the work does not conflict with their Tribune responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek editorial approval before taking outside work that could conflict with Tribune duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top Editors Coordinate with Other Divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Top editors work with other divisions — including marketing, sponsorship and development — to help support, promote and enhance editorial efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such coordination is allowed but should not compromise journalistic independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Promotion of Membership/Fundraising (Voluntary)
rubrics_metrics.description: From time to time, editorial employees may promote Tribune membership drives or fundraising initiatives on their personal social media profiles or be featured in Tribune marketing materials; they do this at their own discretion and are under no obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal participation is voluntary and not required by the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderating/Speaking at Sponsored Events
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial employees may moderate panels or speak at Tribune events underwritten by corporate sponsors, so long as their role is purely journalistic; sponsors do not determine the panelists, the subject matter or the line of questioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain journalistic control of content and participants when participating in sponsored events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honoraria Payment Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Any honoraria must be paid to the Tribune — not to the journalist — in the form of a tax-deductible donation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual journalists should not personally accept speaking fees; payments go to the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and Travel Expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribune employees, contractors and interns will not accept any gift with more than a nominal value from any company, individual or institution that could have an interest in the Tribune’s reporting. We always pay our own way when traveling for editorial or business purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject substantive gifts and personally cover travel to avoid conflicts or the appearance of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Partisan Political Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees, contractors and interns with any responsibility for reporting or editing the news will refrain from partisan political activity of any kind, including making political contributions or displaying partisan signage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff engaged in reporting/editing should avoid overt partisan activity that could compromise perceived impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships and Advertising Distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune accepts corporate sponsorships, underwriting and, within permissible limits, advertising that does not compromise its editorial integrity. All such support, including 'sponsor content,' must be clearly and obviously distinguished from editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor/advertiser content must be visually and textually separable from independent reporting; readers should not confuse sponsorship with editorial content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of Sponsor/Advertiser Content That Undermines Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sponsor or advertiser messages that contain false or unlawful content, or that the Tribune believes undermines its integrity, mission or brand, may be removed at the Tribune’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Tribune reserves the right to reject or remove sponsor content that is inconsistent with its standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business Staff Solicits Corporate Support; No Sponsored Content by Employees
rubrics_metrics.description: All corporate support will be solicited by the Tribune’s business staff, and no sponsored content will be produced by Texas Tribune employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation between business solicitation and editorial production is required; sponsored content production is not done by newsroom staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: TribTalk Editorial Independence and Labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: TribTalk columns were solicited from and authored by thought leaders; no Tribune reporters or editors wrote for or contributed. TribTalk editors had sole discretion to choose submitted columns; sponsors and donors played no role. TribTalk included columns clearly labeled as 'paid placement' and visually differentiated from independent editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion/comment sections should be clearly separated from newsroom reporting; paid placements must be labeled and visually distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Editorial Oversight Required
rubrics_metrics.description: This policy is designed to guide decision-making about AI tools. AI requires journalistic oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI tools cannot be used as a substitute for editorial oversight; decisions about use should be guided by newsroom values and reviewed regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Do Not Replace Journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Tribune will not use AI to replace our journalists, who do essential, original and intensive work gathering and reporting news on politics and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI may assist but not substitute for core reporting functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Restriction on Publishing AI-generated Text
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not publish text generated by AI tools unless it has gone through a rigorous verification and editing process. Journalists will not use information from generative tools as a primary source of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated text must be validated and edited; do not treat generative outputs as primary source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Disclosure of Use to Editors and in Published Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists will disclose to their editors if they used tools such as ChatGPT in the reporting process. When AI tools play a role in developing key findings in a story, we will clearly disclose how the tools were used. If we build products that rely on AI to generate published information, we will disclose the usage and add context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full transparency to editors and readers about AI's role is required, including explanations of how outputs were verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Cautious Experimentation Encouraged for Specific Tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribune journalists may experiment with AI tools for tasks such as data analysis, transcription, headline/SEO and social platform writing, but they must be critical of the tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed uses include production-oriented tasks; journalists must treat outputs skeptically and verify results.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Treat Outputs as Unverified; Independently Verify
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat AI-generated output as unverified information and work to independently verify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always corroborate AI-sourced facts or analysis before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Protect Confidential Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists will avoid putting confidential information such as anonymous source names or privately obtained documents into third-party AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never expose sensitive information to external AI services that may retain or misuse it.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: No AI-generated Images for News; Label Newsworthy AI Images
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not use AI to generate images for news stories. In cases where AI-generated images are the newsworthy subject of a story, we will clearly label them as such with a watermark and caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit AI images in news coverage except when the image itself is the topic, and then label them transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Rights over Site Content and Scraping
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tribune may selectively block some AI technologies from 'scraping' the Tribune website to add training data for their models. We will review these tools on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the costs and benefits of allowing third-party AI indexing of Tribune content and take protective measures as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI: Non-Editorial Staff Use
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools may be used for production of non-journalistic content. Staff on marketing, communications, product, revenue, operations and other non-editorial teams are encouraged to experiment with AI for copywriting assistance, automation of workflows and business efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-editorial staff should discuss and disclose usage with their manager and be attentive to security and accuracy concerns.
